params.body:
## The measured problem

A colleague browsing the shared stock only ever sees a vehicle's **platform photos**: the
duplicated copies with the background removed and the licence plate blurred.
`stocklist/_grid_card.blade.php`, `stocklist/_tabs/general.blade.php` and
`PublicVehicleResource` all read `stocklist_photo` / `primary_stocklist_photo`, and none of
them falls back to the own photo. A vehicle shared without copies is therefore not shown
"with a readable plate" — it is shown **with no photos at all**.

Measured on staging (production data): **828 vehicles are shared, 21 of them have no
platform photo**. Those 21 are sitting invisible in other dealers' listings today. The cause
is not a bug in the code but a step a human has to remember: the copy is made by pressing
"dupliceren", and garage staff forget. Recorded as X-102.

## What now happens on save

`OwnStockService::finalizeCreate` / `finalizeEdit` — the one place every door goes through
(the classic form, the Livewire sheet, the partner API) — asks `PlatformPhotoService` to
queue a copy for every own photo without one, whenever `available_on_stocklist` is on and
the vehicle is not a bidding vehicle. The list button (`OwnStockList::putOnStocklist`) and
"publiceren" on the sheet do the same. The Stocklist checkbox is the signal, so credits are
only spent on vehicles that are actually shared, which is exactly when the copies are needed.

The row and the job are the existing ones (`stocklist = 1`, `processing = 1`,
`ProcessImage::dispatch($id, true)`), so the tiles show the "in verwerking" spinner and the
"worden op de achtergrond verwerkt" note that uploads already use. The dealer gets one
`ui.notify` with the count ("3 platformfoto's worden aangemaakt.") over the same `flash`
event the rest of the sheet uses — no new mechanism.

**All photos, not a selection.** The dealer picks per photo today, but a colleague sees all
or nothing, and clicking away an unwanted copy is one action while discovering an empty
listing is not. This is a deliberate choice, written down as R S2-1.13.

## When it cannot work

- **Credits / a refusal.** remove.bg running out is caught inside `Photo::old_remove_background`
  today (it reports and leaves the blurred-only copy), so the copy still exists. When the job
  genuinely gives up — Blurit refusing, the queue giving up after ten attempts — `ProcessImage::failed()`
  now clears the flag, and a platform copy whose file never arrived is **force**-deleted rather
  than soft-deleted, so it does not read as "the dealer threw it away" and the photo counts as
  missing again.
- **Whatever the reason**, the photo tab carries a line derived from the data:
  "Deze wagen staat gedeeld, maar 3 foto's hebben nog geen platformkopie: collega's zien ze
  niet." That is true for credits, for a refusal, for a queue that never ran, and it is the
  honest signal the old silence lacked (R S2-1.16).
- **The seal.** Outside production `ProcessImage` fakes remove.bg and Blurit, and a faked
  platform copy is a photo *with* a background and a readable plate — which is precisely what a
  platform copy may not be. So when `Outbound::allows('removebg')` or `('blurit')` is closed,
  nothing is created, nothing is queued, and the dealer gets a red notify saying the vehicle is
  shared without photos (R S2-1.14). On production both are always open.

## Not re-duplicating

`vehicle_photos` is soft-deleted, so the schema **can** tell the two apart: a copy the dealer
deleted leaves a row with `deleted_at`, a copy that was never made leaves nothing. The missing
set is computed against `stocklist_photoWithTrashed`, so a deliberately deleted copy is never
recreated. One case cannot be resolved: copies created through the partner API
(`Photo::createStockListPhotoFromPhoto`) carry no `vehicle_photo_id`, so they cannot be matched
to an origin. Such a vehicle is skipped and counted separately rather than guessed at — guessing
means a second copy of a photo that already has one, with the credits on top (R S1-6.26).

## The backlog command

```
php artisan stocklist:platformfotos [--dealer=] [--limit=] [--apply]
```

Default is a dry run: it counts the shared vehicles with missing copies, lists them per
vehicle, and names the cost in remove.bg credits before anything is spent.

```
Gedeelde wagens bekeken: 828
+-------+--------+------------+------------+
| wagen | dealer | ontbrekend | kopieën nu |
+-------+--------+------------+------------+
| 21949 | 137    | 3          | 0          |
+-------+--------+------------+------------+
Wagens met ontbrekende kopieën: 21
Foto's zonder kopie: 84
Kost bij uitvoeren: 84 remove.bg-credits (één per foto).
Droogloop: er is niets gewijzigd. Uitvoeren met --apply.
```

## Tests

`PlatformPhotosOnShareTest` (queue faked, no outbound call): saving with the box on queues one
duplication per missing photo and none for a photo that already has a copy; a copy the dealer
deleted is not made again; saving with the box off queues nothing and says nothing; the notify
carries the right count; the seal closed queues nothing, creates nothing and reports in red; the
command's dry run changes nothing and reports the right number, and `--apply` queues them.

Rules: R S2-1.13 through R S2-1.16 (publishing), R S1-6.26 (photos), finding X-102. Tests carry
`@rule` tags.
params.title: A shared vehicle gets its platform photos by itself
